title: 'What will we have left if we stop loving summer?': Heatwaves crush France's season of insouciance
subhed: The heatwave continues across France, with nearly the entire country under an orange alert on Thursday. The recurrence of extreme temperatures has taken a toll on morale, dampening the usual carefree spirit of summer, as residents of Le Perreux and Nogent-sur-Marne, in the Paris region, explained.

Three men executed by lethal injection on same day in US for the first time since 2010
subhed: Tennessee and Oklahoma put inmates to death within 30 minutes of each other on Thursday. Alabama followed suit hours later. Having three executions in one day is a coincidence in scheduling but it also reflects a trend of increased executions in the US.

title: 'Each time, the suspension of conflict between Israel and its neighbors leaves unanswered the question that caused it'
subhed: In Lebanon, Gaza and Iran, Israel deploys its military power without ever addressing the political issues raised by these conflicts. The decision to always postpone these questions now poses a danger, writes foreign policy analyst Yonatan Touval, in this op-ed for Le Monde.

title: Finland wants to restore its peatlands to help the environment. And to slow Russian tanks.
subhed: The Nordic country has identified 180,000 hectares of wetlands that, if restored, could benefit not only the climate and biodiversity but also national defense. While the military supports the plan, some environmentalists warn against rushing the process.

subhed: The veteran Russian politician, 63, tried to challenge Vladimir Putin's regime and its war in Ukraine through legal and electoral means. He failed. Facing the threat of arrest, he decided to leave Russia. His interview with Le Monde is his first since arriving in France.

title: The long fight to return the 'Ségou treasure,' a spoil of colonization
subhed: The Sufi spiritual leader El Hadj Omar Tall, who counted hundreds of thousands of followers, was a 19th-century scholar and anti-colonialist fighter. France's adoption of a law on the restitution of stolen cultural property could allow his descendants to recover his manuscripts, jewelry, and valuable possessions.

title: 'I can't stand being only breasts. The eyes burn me': Breasts, a tale of men, women and the times
subhed: 'My Breasts and Me' (4/5). Once a symbol of objectifying women, plastic surgery now draws more women practitioners. The #MeToo wave shook up society and patients' expectations have evolved, reshaping boundaries between genders. Le Monde spent weeks behind closed doors in a private breast surgery practice.
